metadata.title: Intel is showing very fast growth in an underrated part of its business - MarketWatch

content.text:
15 hours ago
Intel is showing very fast growth in an underrated part of its business
Intel's claim to fame lies with its central processing units, but the company also makes application-specific integrated circuits, and it's seeing explosive growth in this smaller part of its business.
Intel's CFO David Zinsner said that the company is "probably running at about a $2 billion run rate" or "at least approaching a $2 billion run rate" within ASICs, which are custom chips. Broadcom and Marvell are among the best known makers of ASICs.
In the first quarter, Intel reported it was at a run rate of north of $1 billion. "We think in the not too distant future, we'll be at a $4 billion run rate for that business," Zinsner said on Thursday.
